question:
A geometry class considers the set $T$ of all triangles in a plane. A relation $R$ is defined on $T$ by $T_1RT_2$ if and only if $T_1$ is similar to $T_2$. Four triangles are selected for investigation: triangle $A$ has sides $3,4,5$, triangle $B$ has sides $6,8,10$, triangle $C$ has sides $5,12,13$, and triangle $D$ has sides $9,12,15$. The students compare corresponding side ratios and then analyse the general properties of the relation. Their aim is to determine whether similarity gives a valid equivalence relation on the set of all triangles.

(a) Determine which of the triangles $B,C,D$ are related to triangle $A$.

(b) Verify that $R$ is reflexive.

(c) Show that $R$ is transitive.

(d) Verify that $R$ is symmetric and hence conclude whether $R$ is an equivalence relation.
explanation:
(a)
For triangles $A$ and $B$, the corresponding side ratios are $\frac{6}{3}=\frac{8}{4}=\frac{10}{5}=2$. Hence $A$ and $B$ are similar, so $ARB$. For triangles $A$ and $D$, $\frac{9}{3}=\frac{12}{4}=\frac{15}{5}=3$, so $A$ and $D$ are similar and $ARD$. Triangle $C$ has sides $5,12,13$, which are not proportional to $3,4,5$. Therefore, $A$ is not related to $C$. Thus, among $B,C,D$, the triangles related to $A$ are $B$ and $D$.

(b)
Every triangle has the same shape as itself and its corresponding sides are in the ratio $1:1$. Therefore, every triangle is similar to itself. Hence $TRT$ for every $T\in T$, and the relation is reflexive.

(c)
Suppose $T_1RT_2$ and $T_2RT_3$. Then $T_1$ is similar to $T_2$ and $T_2$ is similar to $T_3$. Therefore, corresponding sides of $T_1$ and $T_2$ are proportional, and corresponding sides of $T_2$ and $T_3$ are proportional. Consequently, corresponding sides of $T_1$ and $T_3$ are also proportional, so $T_1$ is similar to $T_3$. Hence $T_1RT_3$, and $R$ is transitive.

(d)
If $T_1RT_2$, then $T_1$ is similar to $T_2$. Similarity is mutual, so $T_2$ is also similar to $T_1$. Hence $T_2RT_1$, showing that $R$ is symmetric. Since $R$ is reflexive, symmetric and transitive, $R$ is an equivalence relation.

options.A: Only triangle $B$ is related to $A$; $R$ is reflexive and symmetric but not transitive, so it is not an equivalence relation.
options.B: Triangles $B$ and $D$ are related to $A$, while $C$ is not; $R$ is reflexive, symmetric and transitive, so it is an equivalence relation.
options.C: Triangles $B,C$ and $D$ are all related to $A$; $R$ is symmetric and transitive but not reflexive, so it is not an equivalence relation.
options.D: Only triangle $C$ is related to $A$; $R$ is reflexive and transitive but not symmetric, so it is not an equivalence relation.
